summary: BifrOSt has a system audio service (audiod) that owns the speaker and microphone, with playback queue, volume, mute and WAV recording exposed to apps through the SDK audio client. App-level permission and input mute, player pan, rate and volume fades are modelled in the SDK; session categories, interruptions and route notifications are modelled but not wired to audiod. The AVAudioEngine graph, MIDI playback and speech synthesis have no full app-facing counterpart; the output route is switched by the shell alone.

features.note: recording is gated by an explicit user tap in the app (verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 8 tests). The pure model asks for the permission only while it is undetermined, keeps a refusal until settings change it, and queues one event per input mute change; all of it is tested headless. Gap: the shell's prompt and mute switch do not feed the model, so the live permission check needs the lab machine and audiod.
